messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a big prune backlog in ArgoCD around 16:10 UTC, leader flipped twice in 30s and prune wave stalled. GPU app-of-apps are stuck OutOfSync and some node pools report PendingTerminating pods.
ken: re: leader flips — can you paste controller logs? I want to see election events and any rate-limit 429s.
maria: pasted logs below from argocd-controller-0 (shortened):
```
I0318 16:09:58.123456       1 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out
I0318 16:09:58.123500       1 leaderelection.go:183] attempting to acquire leader lease...
I0318 16:09:58.223600       1 controller.go:512] starting prune wave, batch=50
I0318 16:09:59.323700       1 controller.go:520] prune error: rpc error: code=ResourceExhausted desc="apiserver request rate exceeded" status=429
I0318 16:10:28.999900       1 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out
```

ken: API server 429s explain the pruning thrash. Lease renew timeouts + low leaseDuration = leader churn. Looks like the argocd helm values we deployed last week set leaseDuration: 15s.
devon: yeah terraform change that lowered it to 15s to speed failover for control-plane tests. That was fine for control-plane apps but pruning large app-of-apps with thousands of objects spikes request rate.
samir: cost/impact note — GPU node pools were held; autoscaler couldn't drain because terminating pods blocked and some jobs retried. We're burning reserved GPU time while capacity unavailable. We need a short mitigation.
ken: immediate mitigation: 1) pause pruning waves (avoid more API pressure) 2) increase leader leaseDuration and bump operation processors so work is more distributed and less bursty 3) throttle app-of-apps prune batch size.
maria: how do we pause pruning? Is there a quick argocd flag?
ken: can disable prune for a sync by setting --prune to false when doing manual syncs, but for automation, patch argocd-cm to set resource.customizations.health/timeout? Better quick hack: scale argocd-controller to 0 then 1 to force single controlled leader and then temporarily reduce concurrency by patching argocd-cm.
argocd-bot: NOTE: Argo CD detected leader change: new leader argocd-controller-1 at 16:10:31 UTC :bell: 
ops-bot: alert created: infra.argocd.prune_queue_length > 100 (firing) — paging eng-infra on-call.
ken: concrete commands I'm going to run now (dry-run first):
```
# reduce instantaneous prune pressure
kubectl -n argocd patch cm argocd-cm --type merge -p '{"data": {"application.instanceLabelKey":"app.kubernetes.io/instance","resource.customizations": "argoproj.io/Application: { prunePropagationPolicy: 'Background' }"}}'
# increase leader lease duration to 60s in helm values
helm upgrade argocd argo/argo-cd -n argocd --reuse-values --set controller.leaderElection.leaseDuration=60
# temporarily set operation processors
kubectl -n argocd patch deploy argocd-repo-server --patch '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"repo-server","env":[{"name":"ARGOCD_OPS_PROCS","value":"25"}] }]}}}}'
```

devon: note: the helm chart value path might be controller.leaderElection.leaseDurationSeconds depending on chart version — double-check before apply.
maria: ran the patch to lower concurrency of prune batch (set batch size to 20) and bumped lease to 60s via helm (applied as dry-run then real). Observed leader stable for 90s now.
ken: good. Next: we should terraform this change (prevent config drift) — devon, do you want to add the upgraded values back into the argocd helm release in repo-infra?
devon: on it. I'll update modules/argocd/values.yaml with controller.leaderElection.leaseDurationSeconds: 60 and argocd.controller.operationProcessors: 25 and add a comment about prune batch tuning. PR will link to this thread.
samir: monitoring: add a k8s metric to track argocd prune API error rate and leader_election_failures. Also add a dashboard panel for queue length.
ops-bot: infra ticket created: INFRA-2482 "ArgoCD prune backlog causing GPU pool drain" assigned to @devon.
maria: post-mitigation checks: prune queue decreased from 312 -> 12 over 6m, GPU nodes started draining properly, autoscaler released 3 nodes.
ken: follow-ups: - terraform rollback window if we see unexpected behavior - add a small canary to change leaseDuration via feature flag - add runbook step for 'if prune_queue > 200: increase leaseDuration and reduce batch size'
devon: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo-infra/pull/456 — includes values and a short test plan.
maria: thanks all. leaving the alert on for 2h and will update if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
